answer: To stop aliases from capturing trade juries, anchor selection to locked coins rather than names. One coin buys one lottery ticket, held until appeals end. For a dispute over a hollow trellis support, draw jurors using a random seed revealed only after tickets are committed. Splitting 100 tickets across 100 keys leaves the same total selection odds as one key. Greater influence requires more locked capital. The draw must be unpredictable and ticket-based, with no extra chance per identity; wealthy attackers remain a risk.
